scope: UI visual history from the 1980s through 12 October 2026; complements research-sources.json without changing its earlier access record

sources.title: The Xerox Star: a retrospective
sources.supports: Designers date Star's introduction to April 1981 and explain the paper/office metaphor and visual consistency. Inspected figure 1 is the later ViewPoint successor, not a launch screenshot of Star.

sources.title: Lisa source-code preservation announcement
sources.supports: Dates Lisa's launch to 19 January 1983. A release anchor, not a claim that Lisa invented the GUI.

sources.title: First Macintosh press release
sources.supports: Original release date and desktop metaphor. Distinguishes the product introduction from the earlier Super Bowl advertisement.

sources.title: Susan Kare: GUI icon sketches
sources.supports: Dates icon design work to 1982–1983 and explains bitmap constraints. Design-work dates are not the Macintosh launch date.

sources.title: Workbench Nostalgia: release 1.0
sources.supports: Workbench 1.0 shipped with Amiga 1000 in 1985. Do not derive undocumented palette-selection motives from this record.

sources.title: System 1.1 screenshots
sources.supports: Inspected desktop and control panel show monochrome bitmap grammar. This is a later screenshot of historical software; its on-screen clock is not a 1984 publication date.

sources.title: Workbench 1.0 screenshots
sources.supports: Inspected blue/orange limited-palette desktop, bitmap labels and outlined windows. Software-version date differs from screenshot creation.

sources.title: Microsoft's Windows anniversary history
sources.supports: Reproduces the 20 November 1985 retail-shipment announcement. This dates the Windows 1.0 environment, not every early color GUI.

sources.title: MS-DOS and the 1981 PC
sources.supports: A dated personal-computing context for text interfaces. Terminal and character-grid traditions have earlier roots.

sources.title: Mike and Denise Okuda Q&A
sources.supports: Designers date original TNG display panels to 1987 and distinguish believable fictional instrumentation from a complete usable interface.

sources.title: OPEN LOOK archive
sources.supports: 1988–1989 period articles establish an early workstation design context. No original OPEN LOOK manual was fully inspected.

sources.title: Motif FAQ
sources.supports: Dates OSF/Motif's look-and-feel specification to around 1989 and distinguishes toolkit mechanism from visual/behavioral policy.

sources.title: NeXTSTEP and early app history
sources.supports: 1989 NeXTSTEP lineage anchor. It does not validate all screenshot dates or exact visual details of every version.

sources.title: NeXTSTEP release-three interface guidelines
sources.supports: The indexed 1993 manual is a bibliographic lead; the PDF fetch was forbidden and its full contents are not claimed as read.

sources.title: NeXTSTEP 3.0 archive record
sources.supports: Records September 1992 for version 3.0. The record page did not provide an inspected desktop frame.

sources.title: Windows 95 UI case study
sources.supports: Design-team formation in October 1992 and iterative work leading to Windows 95. Development start and release date are distinct.

sources.title: Windows 95 anniversary
sources.supports: Confirms 24 August 1995 launch, Start and taskbar. This does not establish the first use of bevels.

sources.title: Windows 95 screenshots
sources.supports: Inspected gray beveled controls, title bars, nested menu and desktop. Historical software rendered later, not a claim about original screenshot creation.

sources.title: BeOS R5 record and screenshots
sources.supports: R5 is a 2000 anchor. Its inspected short active yellow tab differs from a full-width Windows title bar; it does not establish the first appearance of BeOS tabs.

sources.title: Mac OS 8: Platinum appearance
sources.supports: Native name and control appearance. This manual page is dated 18 July 1997; that is a documentation date, not the OS retail release.

sources.title: Mac OS 8 human interface guidelines
sources.supports: Appearance versus layout and Platinum control guidance. PDF screenshot calls returned text placeholders; visual inspection used the HTML figure instead.

sources.title: The look of Luna
sources.supports: Identifies Luna as the XP visual look. Date of this retrospective is not the language's introduction date.

sources.title: Windows XP is here
sources.supports: Worldwide product availability; announcement, manufacturing release and consumer availability are distinct.

sources.title: Windows visual-design history roundtable
sources.supports: Opaque XP versus glass-like Vista, and typography-led Metro. Inspected images are later published historical illustrations; one Windows 7 image visibly identifies a pre-release build.

sources.title: Aero Glass and the desktop window manager
sources.supports: A dated Vista glass-material implementation anchor. The article is not the style's invention event.

sources.title: Oxygen / KDE 4.0 release
sources.supports: Names Oxygen artwork in the release; rendering technology and a visual language remain separate claims.

sources.title: Breeze / Plasma 5.0 release
sources.supports: Names Breeze, flatter theming, typographic emphasis and a gradual migration. It does not imply every component already used the completed theme.

sources.title: GNOME 3.0 release
sources.supports: Dated GNOME Shell redesign anchor. Adwaita's subsequent changes must not be collapsed into this single release.

sources.title: Libadwaita 1.0
sources.supports: New stylesheet, header bars and adaptive-app context. Toolkit release, visual revision and application adoption are different events.

sources.title: Windows Phone Metro design guide announcement
sources.supports: Native Metro name and signage/type-led intent in a preview guide. Does not imply generic flat UI or community Frutiger Metro.

sources.title: Fluent Design announcement
sources.supports: Explicit design-system announcement. Fluent 2017, Fluent 2 guidance and Windows 11's Mica are separate milestones.

sources.title: Windows 11 design
sources.supports: 2021 design context; named native implementation cannot be inferred solely from a rounded rectangle.

sources.title: Windows 11 materials
sources.supports: Mica is opaque and introduced with Windows 11; Acrylic's translucency differs. Current documentation is not a 2017 launch record.

sources.title: Original iPhone introduction
sources.supports: Multi-touch interface announcement, not the June consumer-availability date or the birth of all skeuomorphic UI.

sources.title: Big Sur design introduction
sources.supports: Apple's named visual redesign; depth and rounded controls do not automatically make every component neumorphic.

sources.title: Material Design introduction
sources.supports: Tactile surfaces, graphics and motion as a system; this is not merely flat rendering.

sources.title: Material Design eras
sources.supports: Distinguishes 2014 launch, the 2018 overhaul and later evolution. A source for system eras, not a popularity survey.

sources.title: Android 12 / Material You announcement
sources.supports: Announced personal/adaptive design language and Android beta. Announcement is distinct from adoption across products.

sources.title: Material 3 Expressive announcement
sources.supports: Dated official expressive UI plate. Inspected only a visible portion with timers, messages, clock and controls; motion and actual task performance were not tested.

sources.title: Apple Vision Pro / visionOS announcement
sources.supports: A native spatial-UI milestone; 2023 announcement is not 2024 commercial availability or the beginning of all spatial interfaces.

sources.title: Web Design Museum: 1990s web
sources.supports: Dated archived sites rather than contemporary guesses about 1990s web design. Individual archive captures can differ from a site's launch.

sources.title: GeoCities 1995
sources.supports: Portal/community-hosting anchor. The service homepage is not representative of every personal site it hosted.

sources.title: Grunge in web design
sources.supports: Concrete 1996 and later web examples predate 2008 trend commentary; the name is not a requirement for disorder throughout a page.

sources.title: The Museum of Dirt 1996
sources.supports: Inspected distressed type and bottle collage in a restrained centered page. Specific treatments coexist; grunge need not fill every region.

sources.title: Pixel art in web design
sources.supports: 1996–2005 web examples; pixel art and low-resolution controls have older roots.

sources.title: eBoy 1999
sources.supports: Inspected pixel-built characters, type and texture within actual navigational structure. A static frame does not prove game behavior.

sources.title: Metalheart in web design
sources.supports: Specific 2000–2003 web examples strengthen the UI connection beyond art moodboards. Individual entries still need their own visual inspection.

sources.title: 2Advanced v1, 2000
sources.supports: Inspected technical labels, framed controls and blue layered imagery. Flash and Techno are source categories; a still cannot verify its animation.

sources.title: Eric Jordan / 2Advanced account
sources.supports: Studio founded in 1999 and its immersive Flash practice. Agency founding is not the date all its interface versions debuted.

sources.title: Apple website 2001
sources.supports: Inspected product-led whitespace with dimensional tabs and cards. Clean organization and planar rendering differ; archive link supplies a separate capture timestamp.

sources.title: Google homepage 1998
sources.supports: Inspected sparse task-led structure with a dimensional logo and native controls. A minimal composition is not wholly flat; this is an example date, not minimalism's origin.

sources.title: New York Times website 1996
sources.supports: Inspected newspaper masthead, ruled columns, section navigation and ranked stories. Editorial purpose and editorial aesthetic need independent evidence.

sources.title: Winamp Skin Museum: creator account
sources.supports: A real interface-skin corpus and browser preservation work. The 2020 museum publication must not be used as the birth of 1990s player skins.

sources.title: CSS Zen Garden: creator's account
sources.supports: 2003 project context and deliberate alternate presentations. CSS is an implementation mechanism supporting many aesthetics, not an aesthetic itself.

sources.title: Grunge / Web 2.0 contemporary commentary
sources.supports: Describes 2007 gloss/rounded/reflection vocabulary and a textural reaction. Commentary date does not override the museum's earlier grunge examples.

sources.title: Poolside FM redesign
sources.supports: A 2019 browser UI intentionally remixes 1980s/1990s desktop reference worlds. The title's 1986 is fiction/reference time, not the website's release.

sources.title: Original neumorphism article
sources.supports: Original visible publication date and naming discussion; full member-only text was not read. Secondary references giving 16 December are not preferred over this displayed date.

sources.title: Glassmorphism generator: naming history
sources.supports: Author dates his terminology article to November 2020. This is a naming/publication milestone, not the invention of translucent UI.

sources.title: Glassmorphism article illustration
sources.supports: Inspected translucent concept card over colored forms. It is an illustrative treatment, not independently verified production banking UI.

sources.title: Claymorphism creator video
sources.supports: Dated creator terminology description. Video playback/transcript was unavailable; unread content is not claimed.

sources.title: Claymorphism article illustration
sources.supports: Inspected puffy dashboard mockups and tactile rendering. It is a conceptual illustration, not a tested production dashboard.

sources.title: Gumroad rebrand announcement
sources.supports: Dates brand/website/font/color change. Its visual style requires separate evidence; the public post body did not render in the browser reader.

sources.title: Brutalism and antidesign
sources.supports: Distinguishes stripped-down presentation from deliberate convention-breaking and includes a 2000/2001 precedent. Not proof of a single first coiner.

sources.title: Memphis-Milano
sources.supports: 1980s design influence. Furniture/graphic origins do not demonstrate a coherent 1980s GUI implementation.

sources.title: Frasurbane
sources.supports: Late-1980s/mid-1990s visual context. UI adaptation remains a separate evidence requirement.

sources.title: Global Village Coffeehouse
sources.supports: Late-1980s/1990s hand-drawn consumer/graphic language. No original interface was visually inspected under this label.

sources.title: Utopian Scholastic
sources.supports: Late-1980s/1990s edutainment/collage context. Its Encarta-related alias does not establish that all encyclopedia interfaces share the style.

sources.title: Laser Grid
sources.supports: 1980s high-tech graphic references and 2021 retrospective renaming. Influences on retro-futures differ from production UI evidence.

sources.title: Superflat Pop
sources.supports: Late-2000s/early-2010s pop-graphic context. Not an alias for flat UI or proof of its first UI use.

sources.title: TRON: Legacy graphics
sources.supports: Dated 2010 fictional-screen/motion-graphics work. Film instrumentation can inspire visual UI without proving usable interaction.

sources.title: PalmPilot collection record
sources.supports: 1996 handheld anchor. Native mobile task constraints predate the 2007 iPhone; this record is not a full application audit.

sources.title: Microsoft Bob announcement history
sources.supports: Dates announcement to 7 January 1995. Room metaphors are interface context, not an automatic quality endorsement or generic visual-material alias.
